claim: Let \(p>0\), \(n\ge 1\), and equip \(\mathbb C^n\) with the finite weak-Lorentz quasi-norm \(\|x\|_{p,\infty,n}=\max_{1\le k\le n} k^{1/p}x_k^*\), where \(x_1^*\ge\cdots\ge x_n^*\) is the decreasing rearrangement of the coordinate moduli. For \(u\in\mathbb C^n\), define \(G_u(x)=(x_1,\ldots,x_n,\sum_{j=1}^n u_jx_j)\in\mathbb C^{n+1}\). If \(u_1^*\ge\cdots\ge u_n^*\) rearranges \((|u_j|)\), then \(G_u\) is a linear isometry from \(\ell_{p,\infty}^n\) into \(\ell_{p,\infty}^{n+1}\) if and only if \(\sum_{k=1}^n k^{-1/p}u_k^*\le (n+1)^{-1/p}\). Equivalently, the appended functional has exact operator gauge \(\sup_{\|x\|_{p,\infty,n}\le1}|\sum_j u_jx_j|=\sum_{k=1}^n k^{-1/p}u_k^*\), and the graph is isometric exactly when this gauge does not exceed \((n+1)^{-1/p}\). For \(n\ge2\), such an isometry fails to preserve disjointness of coordinate vectors exactly when at least two coefficients \(u_j\) are nonzero. Among isometric graph maps, the largest possible common overlap \(\min_j|u_j|\) is \((n+1)^{-1/p}/\sum_{k=1}^n k^{-1/p}\), attained when all coefficient moduli are equal; at \(n=2\) this recovers the coefficient in Fang--Gao--Huang--Sukochev, Remark 1.1.

correctness.rationale: For every \(p>0\), the unit-ball inequalities \(x_k^*\le k^{-1/p}\) and rearrangement give the exact functional gauge, with equality at a phase-aligned vector. Sufficiency follows by counting how many target coordinates can exceed each weak-Lorentz threshold after appending a coordinate of size at most \( (n+1)^{-1/p}\|x\|\). Necessity uses the same extremizer: all original coordinates exceed the last target threshold, so an appended value above it would force the target quasi-norm above one. The disjointness and balanced-overlap statements then follow exactly. No convexity assumption or finite experiment is used.

The new statement is an iff characterization of the whole one-functional graph family for every finite dimension, plus the exact disjointness and balanced-overlap boundaries. Targeted semantic searches returned no statement implying this classification. The residual risk is an older finite-dimensional Lorentz-space embedding result under different terminology.

value.rationale: The focal paper uses a single two-dimensional nonsurjective example to justify why surjectivity is essential for its disjointness theory. The finding gives the natural complete classification of that canonical one-extra-coordinate mechanism in every finite dimension, identifies exactly when disjointness fails, and computes the largest possible uniform shared-coordinate contamination. This is a structural boundary theorem for the motivating obstruction, not merely a recomputation of the published coefficient.
